points.en: IPR refers to legal rights given to inventors and creators for their intellectual creations.
points.hi: IPR refers to legal rights given to inventors and creators for their intellectual creations.

points.en: Types: Patents (inventions), Copyrights (literary/artistic works), Trademarks (brand identity), Geographical Indications (origin-based quality).
points.hi: Types: Patents (inventions), Copyrights (literary/artistic works), Trademarks (brand identity), Geographical Indications (origin-based quality).

points.en: TRIPS Agreement: WTO agreement setting minimum standards for IPR regulation globally.
points.hi: TRIPS Agreement: WTO agreement setting minimum standards for IPR regulation globally.

points.en: National IPR Policy 2016: 'Creative India; Innovative India'.
points.hi: National IPR Policy 2016: 'Creative India; Innovative India'.

points.en: Nodal Agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
points.hi: Nodal Agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

points.en: Patent Act 1970: Governs patentability, including Section 3(d) which prevents evergreening.
points.hi: Patent Act 1970: Governs patentability, including Section 3(d) which prevents evergreening.

explanation.en: P for Patents, C for Copyrights, T for Trademarks, G for Geographical Indications.
explanation.hi: P for Patents, C for Copyrights, T for Trademarks, G for Geographical Indications.

question.en: What is the primary objective of the TRIPS Agreement?
question.hi: What is the primary objective of the TRIPS Agreement?

answer.en: To harmonize IPR protection standards across WTO member nations to facilitate international trade.
answer.hi: To harmonize IPR protection standards across WTO member nations to facilitate international trade.

misconception.en: IPR is only for large corporations.
misconception.hi: IPR is only for large corporations.

correction.en: IPR is crucial for startups and MSMEs to protect their innovations and gain competitive advantage.
correction.hi: IPR is crucial for startups and MSMEs to protect their innovations and gain competitive advantage.

fiveFacts.en: India is a signatory to the Paris Convention and the Patent Cooperation Treaty.
fiveFacts.hi: India is a signatory to the Paris Convention and the Patent Cooperation Treaty.

fiveFacts.en: Copyright protection generally lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years.
fiveFacts.hi: Copyright protection generally lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years.

fiveFacts.en: Geographical Indications are registered under the GI of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.
fiveFacts.hi: Geographical Indications are registered under the GI of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.

fiveFacts.en: The Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (CGPDTM) administers IPR laws in India.
fiveFacts.hi: The Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (CGPDTM) administers IPR laws in India.

fiveFacts.en: Evergreening of patents is restricted under Section 3(d) of the Indian Patents Act.
fiveFacts.hi: Evergreening of patents is restricted under Section 3(d) of the Indian Patents Act.

threeTraps.en: Assuming all IPRs are perpetual (most have expiry dates).
threeTraps.hi: Assuming all IPRs are perpetual (most have expiry dates).

threeTraps.en: Confusing Trademarks with Patents (Trademarks protect brands, Patents protect inventions).
threeTraps.hi: Confusing Trademarks with Patents (Trademarks protect brands, Patents protect inventions).

threeTraps.en: Ignoring the role of the judiciary in IPR enforcement.
threeTraps.hi: Ignoring the role of the judiciary in IPR enforcement.
